scope: Theorem 3.4 (Pathwise detection and approximation) of the manuscript “Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions” (preprints/Quasipolynomial-Bounds-for-Arithmetic-Progressions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 159 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 481eaf7730dc4d58), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 22. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Prescribe finitely many testing degrees in the fixed allowed range, local test complexities, slice costs, input caps, and accuracies. The later parameters of the one-layer construction can be chosen once so that the following assertions hold for this same ensemble, uniformly in the center and the site input. For cold-pre requests, if a cold-pre-bounded input satisfies Xr(g) ≥ a > 0, with log(1/a) bounded by cold-pre data, then g correlates in uniform parent measure with an ambient atom of cold-pre complexity, and the logarithm of the reciprocal correlation has a cold-pre bound. Every |g| ≤ 1 can also be approximated in Xr, to the prescribed cold-pre accuracy, by a linear combination of such atoms with cold-pre coefficient mass and number of terms. If r < j and the requests are warm, every warm-bounded input with Xr(g) ≥ a > 0 and a warm bound for log(1/a) correlates in µc with an ambient atom of warm complexity, with a warm bound for the logarithm of the reciprocal correlation. The atoms, coefficient mass, and number of terms in the Xr approximation also have warm bounds. These bounds may use the omission threshold but do not use Qj or the height of W. For a specified larger input cap, include its logarithm in the request budget and rescale. Increasing the requested accuracy, test, or path budgets changes the corresponding warm or cold-pre output logarithms polynomially. All path probabilities and testing suprema refer to the law before productive paths are selected.
